item.title: Kalu mourns late Afenifere leader, Fasoranti
item.description: Former Abia State Governor and Senator representing Abia North, Orji Uzor Kalu, has expressed condolences to the family of late elder statesman and Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, who died at the age of 100. Kalu described the late Yoruba leader as a respected statesman who devoted much of his life to the service of humanity, national unity and Nigeria’s development. In a statement he signed on Tuesday, the senator said Fasoranti lived a long and fulfilled life marked by patriotism, selfless service and commitment to democratic ideals. “Pa Fasoranti lived a long and fulfilled life marked by patriotism, selfless service and commitment to the unity and progress of Nigeria. “His contributions to democracy, good governance and national development will remain part of his enduring legacy,” Kalu said. The former governor extended his condolences to the deceased’s family, the leadership of Afenifere, the government and people of Ondo State, and the Yoruba nation. He urged the family to take solace in Fasoranti’s remarkable life and enduring contributions to the country. Kalu also prayed for the peaceful repose of the late elder statesman’s soul and asked God to grant his family the strength to bear the loss. item.title: Fernandes takes aim at Carrick as Man Utd lurch into fresh crisis
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes criticised manager Michael Carrick’s tactics following the humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como. United fell behind to a second-minute goal and never recovered as the club’s winless run reached seven games after another lacklustre performance. “We started on the wrong foot and they scored very early,” Fernandes told TNT Sports. “Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way.” The Portugal midfielder suggested Nico Paz’s early strike for Como on Wednesday night had a damaging effect on the visitors, leaving them struggling to impose themselves. Paz scored again after Tasos Douvikas had doubled the lead, with Jacobo Ramon adding a fourth. Only a stoppage-time goal from Joshua Zirkzee stopped United from succumbing to their joint-heaviest Champions League loss. “Conceding early makes us go into the game with a mood of defeat,” said Fernandes. “It’s difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. “If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation.” Fernandes also highlighted United’s passive approach out of possession, saying Como were allowed too much time and space to dictate play. Asked whether those comments amounted to criticism of Carrick’s tactics, Fernandes said: “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me. “Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.” Fernandes is the latest United player to publicly break ranks. Defender Lisandro Martinez took aim at the club’s hierarchy following a 2-0 Champions League loss to Atletico Madrid last week. Martinez said Carrick had been left with an understrength squad. He later apologised. Youri Tielemans, who started alongside Fernandes in the United midfield in Italy, admitted the display was simply not good enough. “We got outplayed for most of the game so it was a very disappointing night,” said Tielemans. “You can be good tactically but if the effort is not good (then it will not work) and vice versa. You need to be good at everything and tonight we were poor.” AFP The post Fernandes takes aim at Carrick as Man Utd lurch into fresh crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

Responding, the lawyer said he relied on Section 36 of the 1999 Constitution. Oladunjoye also countered Ekwe’s submission. In a short ruling, the judge agreed with the DSS lawyer’s submission. The judge, who directed the trial to commence and the witness to be co-named as “AB”, ordered that anyone who runs foul of Section 232(5) of ACJA will be liable to one year jail term. Geoffrey Uwadiegwu, counsel to the 3rd and 4th defendants, informed the court that he was coming into the matter for the first and and that he would need more time to study the case file. The prosecution lawyer responded that though Ekwe was just being served with the video evidence, the video clip would not be used in today’s trial. She prayed the court to allow the matter to proceed. Oladunjoye argued that Ekwe’s absence on October 6 caused the case to be adjourned. Dissatisfied, Ekwe and Uwadiegwu stood up at the same time to address court on why the matter must be adjourned. But the judge cautioned them against unruly behaviour in her court. “I run my court in line with international best practice, and that is why people say I am strict. “So, when I run my court, there should be 99.9 per cent compliance according to international best practice,” she said. Justice Abdulmalik said she wouldn’t have listed the case for hearing because there were many pre-election cases in the docket of the court. She added that she had at least nine judgments to write in respect of pre-election matters which must be delivered before Nov. 9. The judge, however, said that she saw the case as very crucial and which should be determined expeditiously. Having listened to the parties, Justice Abdulmalik agreed to give a short adjournment. Suspects The suspects, Michael Okafor, a.k.a Onyechimeleze; Chinedu Chukwudozie, alias Kante; Chibunna Olisa; and Chigozie Olisa, a.k.a Ability were arraigned before Justice Abdulmalik on 28 September on a six-count charge bordering on terrorism and kidnapping. The prosecution alleged that the defendants conspired to commit acts of terrorism and were involved in the abduction of Owoh, while he was travelling from Port Harcourt in Rivers to Awka in Anambra. They were further accused of taking the operative hostage and causing his death in the course of the alleged criminal operation. The suspects were also accused of belonging to the proscribed IPOB and its armed wing, the Eastern Security Network (ESN), as well as involvement in activities allegedly linked to terrorism. In addition, the prosecution alleged that the suspects were involved in the unlawful possession of firearms, including AK-47 and pump-action rifles, in connection with the alleged offences. item.title: NIMASA detains four vessels over Cabotage breaches
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) has intensified enforcement of the Cabotage regime, detaining vessels found to have violated the country’s coastal shipping regulations as part of efforts to ensure compliance with local content requirements in the maritime sector. The operation which focused on vessels of interest identified through intelligence and surveillance profiling led to the arrest and detention of several vessels for nonconformity including MT HOLMES, MT FUJAIRAH ENERGY, JS GRATITUDE, MT BORA within the Lagos maritime domain. Some of the vessels which have regularised their infractions have since been release. Operation Sea Guardian was conducted as a follow-up enforcement initiative aimed at strengthening regulatory compliance, verifying cabotage obligations, assessing surcharge and levy compliance, and ensuring adherence to applicable maritime regulations. It deployed Deep Blue assets to help track, board, inspect, and verify the operational status of vessels identified through intelligence reports and compliance indicators through effective inter-agency cooperation among NIMASA enforcement personnel, the Nigerian Navy, the Maritime Guard Command and C4i intelligence personnel. Reacting to the development, the Director General of NIMASA, Dr. Dayo Mobereola emphasised that such operations are going to be more frequent and that defaulting operators would face the full wrath of the law. According to him, “we had earlier served notice of enhanced enforcement of indigenous participation in our coastal and inland trade and this is exactly what we are doing. It is therefore in the interest of operators to ensure total compliance because defaulters will be visited with stiff sanctions in line with the law”. item.title: NTEL targets cheaper roaming, wider broadband access with WakaGo, AirFibre
item.description: By Juliet Umeh NATCOM Development and Investment Limited, trading as NTEL, has said its WakaGo global eSIM and AirFibre wireless broadband services will help Nigerian travellers reduce roaming costs and expand internet access for businesses and underserved communities. The company said it was leveraging the two products, alongside infrastructure sharing and existing telecommunications assets, to rebuild its network and improve connectivity across Nigeria. Speaking in an interview with Vanguard, NTEL’s Chief Technology Officer, Kingsley Uwazie, said WakaGo was designed to keep Nigerians connected while travelling abroad without purchasing local SIM cards at their destinations. “WakaGo is a global eSIM service designed to help Nigerians travelling abroad stay connected without having to buy a local SIM card at their destination or remove their existing SIM card. “The service enables users with compatible devices to access mobile data for internet services, including WhatsApp calls and messaging, while retaining their primary SIM cards for regular calls. “WakaGo operates on a pay-as-you-go basis, allowing customers to pay for their usage without being locked into a particular country or fixed bundle. “It allows Nigerians to stay connected to their loved ones locally. And the rates are very fair when you compare WakaGo to our competitors out there. “When I say fair, I mean fair against roaming charges, better than the existing roaming charges,” he explained. Uwazie cited customer experiences in Japan, the United States and China as evidence of the service’s potential, including a traveller who used WakaGo to make a video call from a crowded stadium in New York. It also did not indicate that any of the 46 identified contacts had tested positive for Ebola. FAAN Heightens Vigilance Across Airports The development came after FAAN, on Wednesday, said it was maintaining heightened vigilance across airport operations. It said it is working with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), Port Health Services, Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) and other relevant agencies to support ongoing containment efforts. The agency stated that early identification of the case and commencement of contact tracing underscore the importance of established public health protocols, effective surveillance and inter-agency collaboration in responding to potential health threats. “FAAN is maintaining heightened vigilance across airport operations and will continue to coordinate with public health authorities, align its response with further guidance and support additional measures considered necessary to safeguard passengers, airport personnel and the wider public,” it said in a statement by the Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection, Henry Agbebire. It urged passengers, airport users, airlines and other stakeholders to remain calm, vigilant and cooperative with health officials. “The public is also advised to rely on verified information and avoid spreading unconfirmed reports,” it added. “FAAN reassures the travelling public of its continued readiness to work with relevant agencies to protect public health and support the safe operation of Nigeria’s airports.” The Federal Government confirmed a case of the virus in the FCT on Wednesday. FG Assures Nigerians Of Containment Strategies The Presidential Task Force on Ebola Preparedness, Virus Disease Preparedness and Emerging Public Health Threats has assured Nigerians it can handle Ebola in the country. The Chairman of the Task Force and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, said this while speaking to newsmen after the group’s emergency meeting at the State House on Wednesday. Gbajabiamila said the Task Force has been working behind the scenes since it was inaugurated in June this year. He added that this is why it was easy to detect the index case discovered yesterday. “It’s very important to note this. Since the issue of Ebola came up in June, there have been about 44, 000 flights in and out of Nigeria. So, it’s because of what the Ministry of Health, the task force and all the agencies have been doing. All hands have been on deck. “The passenger with the disease showed no symptoms, which came four days after the woman got into Abuja, and it was the identification process and the protocols that were put in place that enabled the quick identification. That also speaks to the country’s capacity and ability to deal with this disease as best as we can,” he said, according to a statement by presidential spokesman Bayo Onanuga. He assured Nigerians that the Task Force would strengthen whatever needed strengthening, the protocols, and ensure more rigorous enforcement moving forward. “The Task Force is on top of it. NCDC is on top of it; everyone is on deck. We must build community trust and avoid panic, but it’s also important to state clearly that this is a collaborative effort between the government and the people. item.title: Standard Chartered names Adelagun CEO
item.description: By Kingsley Adegboye Standard Chartered Bank Nigeria Limited has confirmed Ayodeji Adelagun as its Chief Executive Officer following regulatory approval by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). Adelagun has served as acting CEO since January 2026. He brings more than 26 years of banking and financial markets experience across Africa to the role. Since joining Standard Chartered in 2007, he has held several senior positions, including Executive Director and Head of Markets for Nigeria and Africa, and Head of Rates and Credit Trading for West Africa. He is also Chairman of Standard Chartered Capital and Advisory Nigeria and Head of Markets, Africa. Commenting on his appointment, Adelagun said Nigeria remained a significant long-term growth market for the bank. He stated: “Nigeria represents a significant long-term opportunity for Standard Chartered, and our ambition is to build on the strength of our franchise to deliver even greater value for our clients and the wider economy. “As we enter this next chapter, my focus will be on deepening our client relationships, driving disciplined and sustainable growth, and bringing the full strength of Standard Chartered’s international network and capabilities to clients in Nigeria.” A Fellow of the Financial Markets Dealers Association (FMDA), Adelagun led the workstream that introduced benchmark bonds in Nigeria, helping deepen the domestic bond market and support the country’s inclusion in the JP Morgan Emerging Markets Index. He also pioneered bond trading desks at FSDH and Standard Chartered Bank. Earlier in his career, he worked in Banking Operations, Commercial Banking and Treasury at Access Bank Plc. item.title: FG approves 4 new channel management firms for seaports
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Federal Executive Council (FEC) has approved four new channel management companies for seaports across the country in a move aimed at improving vessel navigation and port operations. Speaking at the recently concluded Annual General Meeting of the Nigerian Association of Master Mariners (NAMM), former General Manager, Marine and Operations, Capt. Ebubeogu Ihenacho, disclosed that there would be changes in the ownership of the Lagos Channel Management Company Limited and the Bonny Channel Management Company. Although Vanguard could not independently ascertain the identities of the new owners, sources close to the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) said a Belgian company is expected to take over channel management operations at the Lagos ports. According to Ihenacho, the four channels serving Nigeria’s major port clusters will have different channel management companies as approved by the FEC. He said a new company had been approved to manage the Lagos port channel, with a change of name, while the Calabar Channel would be managed by the Calabar Channel Management Company. He added that the Bonny Channel Management Company had also undergone a change of ownership. On the Warri Channel, Ihenacho said the Federal Government had approved China Harbour Engineering Company (CHEC) and two other companies to form a consortium to manage the Escravos Channel. He said: “For Warri, it was approved for China Harbour Engineering Company, CHEC, and two other companies, who would now form a consortium. That consortium will now form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) with the Nigerian Ports Authority to manage the Escravos Channel.” Recall that the management of the NPA had declined to renew the concessions of the Lagos Channel Management Company Limited and the Bonny Channel Management Company, opting instead for six-month extensions of the existing arrangements. item.title: Landing cost of petrol falls to N1,283.81/litre
item.description: •As crude oil rises to $108.90 per barrel By Ediri Ejoh The landing cost of imported Premium Motor Spirit, PMS, also known as petrol, has dropped marginally to N1,283.81 per litre from N1,292.88 per litre. The latest figure was disclosed by the Major Energies Marketers Association of Nigeria, MEMAN, in its energy bulletin yesterday. The decline came as Brent crude rose marginally to $108.90 per barrel from $108.80 per barrel, according to figures contained in the report. The latest landing cost is N66.19, or about 4.90 per cent, below Dangote Refinery’s gantry price of N1,350 per litre. Similarly, the landing cost of imported petrol was between N64.19 and N74.19 per litre below the ex-depot prices of N1,348 to N1,358 quoted by depot owners. Despite the decline in landing cost, petrol prices remained elevated in parts of the country, with motorists in Lagos and Abuja reportedly paying between N1,370 and N1,429 per litre at filling stations. The difference between landing costs and pump prices reflects additional costs and margins across the supply chain, including transportation, storage and retail operations. The development comes amid the Federal Government’s proposed 30-day petrol discount at NNPC Limited filling stations. Recall that the Minister of Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, on October 8 proposed that petrol be sold at N1,350 per litre at NNPC Limited outlets under the planned discount initiative. However, the proposed discount had yet to be implemented at NNPC Limited filling stations as of the time of reporting. item.title: Insurance firms’ N300b stuck at CBN over verification for illicit funds
item.description: By Rosemary Iwunze Insurance companies are now struggling to have access to the new capital they raised, amounting to about N300 billion under the just concluded recapitalization programme. The funds were held in the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, pending verifications for illicit funds inflows. Vanguard learnt that following suspicion of possible illicit sources of some of the new investments in the firms the apex imposed stricter capital verification regime, a development which has proved tough for most of the insurance firms to scale through. It is further learnt that while the National Insurance Commission, NAICOM, has given approval for the apex bank to release the funds to the insurers, the affected firms are painstakingly going through the processes. Speaking to journalist during the virtual press briefing on the outcome of the Insurers Committee meeting, Chairman of Nigeria Insurers Association, NIA, Mrs. Ebelechukwu Nwachukwu, stated that, the insurance sector regulator has done its part while operators are currently working on the CBN criteria to access the funds on or before the end of this month. The insurers said they had planned to deploy the new capital in the third quarter of this year to boost their financial performance in 2026 while rewarding their investors with good returns in dividend for their support in the recapitalization program. Recall that the 24 insurance companies had cumulatively raised N300 billion during the exercise, added to over N700 billion existing capital, taking the total industry capital to N1.079 trillion, post recapitalisation. The Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act (NIIRA), 2025, had stipulated that the underwriting firms and reinsurers who participated in the recapitalisation exercise that ended on July 31st, 2026 must keep their recapitalised funds in an escrow account with CBN. Of the 50 firms that scaled through the recapitalisation hurdle, 24 of them raised fresh capital while 26 of them had earlier surpassed the minimum capital benchmark. NIIRA had mandated life underwriters to recapitalise from N2billion to N10billion, non-life from N3billion to N15billion while reinsurers were required to upgrade from N10billion to N35billion. The Commissioner for Insurance/CEO, NAICOM, Mr. Olusegun Omosehin, had earlier disclosed that the capital in the market has now risen to N1.079trillion, up from about N700billion before the exercise. According to him, NAICOM now wants to allow operators access the recapitalisation funds, he promised that the regulator would monitor the operators to ensure that the funds fulfill its purpose and not mismanaged or divested into something else. item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for the N10 billion announced for Ebola preparedness, alleging that the confirmed case in Abuja exposed serious gaps in surveillance and the protection of health workers. Atiku said the government must explain how the emergency funds were spent and why the response allegedly left frontline health workers without adequate protective equipment. He also warned against using the outbreak to restrict political campaigns and voter participation. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, on Wednesday, Atiku demanded a public audit of the funds and answers over the handling of the case. “Where is the money? Publish the amount actually disbursed, the dates of payment, every contract awarded, every recipient and every item delivered. A press statement cannot replace an audit,” he said. Atiku said the patient arrived in Nigeria on October 5, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital on October 11, but the government did not publicly confirm the case until October 20. “During that critical period, 44 close contacts were left unmonitored, while private health workers faced the case without adequate protective equipment. This is a failure of preparedness with potentially grave consequences,” he said. He also questioned the Presidential Task Force announced by Tinubu in June and chaired by his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, insisting that medical experts should lead the response. “Political titles cannot trace contacts, equip hospitals or save lives,” Atiku said. The former vice president further alleged that the planned press conference by the Minister of Health on Thursday was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies and voting. “The Tinubu administration must not weaponise Ebola to frighten the public, silence its opponents or suppress voter participation. Any public health measure must be backed by clear medical evidence, applied equally and never used as a pretext to interfere with Nigerians’ democratic rights,” he said. Atiku urged the government to account for the N10 billion, protect health workers and trace all contacts, warning against turning a public health emergency into a tool for political suppression. item.title: Ebola patient arrived Abuja Oct. 3 via Ethiopian Airlines from Uganda – Source
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Fresh facts emerged, yesterday, regarding the travel itinerary of the confirmed Ebola virus patient in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, revealing that the index case entered Nigeria aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight earlier this month. Read Also: No vaccine, specific treatment for Ebola strain in Nigeria — WHO A highly-placed aviation official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, as she was not authorised to brief the media on the matter, told Vanguard that the patient arrived in the country on October 3, 2026. This is even as the Ugandan government asked Nigeria to provide detailed travel and clinical records of the woman, the index case, insisting she didn’t pick the virus in its territory, since there is no Ebola case in Uganda. According to the aviation official, the patient landed at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, aboard Ethiopian Airlines Flight ET333. The revelation provides critical details for contact-tracing, following an earlier official announcement by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Pate, who confirmed the presence of the virus in the nation’s capital. Pate had disclosed that the female patient had recently returned to Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda and subsequently spent several days receiving care at a private hospital in Abuja before the infection was formally diagnosed. She has since been transferred to a designated isolation facility where she is currently receiving treatment. In response, a multi-agency operation involving the Federal Ministry of Health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, and the FCT Health and Environmental Services Secretariat has commenced extensive contact-tracing. Public health authorities have so far identified 44 close contacts, including healthcare personnel, fellow hospital patients, caregivers and individuals connected to her travel route. Consequently, the Federal Government has placed health institutions and port health surveillance units across the country on high alert. The affected students were taken to the State Hospital, Ijebu-Ode, the General Hospital, Ijebu-Igbo, and other healthcare facilities for medical attention. Among the schools reportedly affected were Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode, and Itamerin Comprehensive High School, Ago-Iwoye. A video circulating on social media showed some students fainting and being rushed for medical attention as panic spread across the affected communities. The incident has renewed concerns over recurring gaseous emissions in parts of Ijebu land, with residents and school authorities calling on the state government to establish the source and prevent further exposure. A teacher in one of the affected schools, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the incident began at about 10 a.m., when students and staff started experiencing breathing difficulties. “The students and staff started inhaling the gas and began to have difficulty breathing. item.title: Senate rejects NMDPRA’s PMS import records, summons agency heads
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate Committee on Public Accounts has rejected the volume of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) imports reported by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) for 2022 and 2023 over significant discrepancies with figures supplied by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL). The committee, chaired by Senator Ahmed Wadada Dankwambo, resolved on Wednesday to summon the heads of NMDPRA, NNPCL and the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (NEITI) to explain the discrepancies and reconcile the conflicting records. The decision followed the NMDPRA’s response to queries raised against it in the NEITI Oil and Gas Industry Audit Report covering 2021 to 2023. Appearing before the committee, the NMDPRA’s Authority Chief Executive, Mallam Rabiu Abdullahi Umar, was represented by Deputy Director Uzoamaka Ugwu-Ojobe, who maintained that the authority’s records were credible despite the differences. She told the committee that NMDPRA recorded 3.29 billion litres of PMS imports in 2022 and 6.02 billion litres in 2023, compared with the 6.27 billion litres and 3.88 billion litres reported by NNPCL for the respective years. “The slight disparities are being looked into for possible reconciliation,” she said. However, Senator Abdul Ningi, representing Bauchi Central, rejected the description of the differences as slight, noting that the figures showed substantial variations that required serious investigation. “The disparities in records of PMS importation between NMDPRA and NNPCL in 2022 and 2023, as stated in the NEITI Oil and Gas Industry Audit Report of 2021 to 2023, are too wide to be described as slight or being looked into without the seriousness required,” he said. Similarly, Senator Dayo Faduyile, representing Ondo South, said the discrepancies raised concerns about the reliability of the records submitted by the two agencies. item.content:encoded: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate Committee on Public Accounts has rejected the volume of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) imports reported by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) for 2022 and 2023 over significant discrepancies with figures supplied by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL). The committee, chaired by Senator Ahmed Wadada Dankwambo, resolved on Wednesday to summon the heads of NMDPRA, NNPCL and the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (NEITI) to explain the discrepancies and reconcile the conflicting records. The decision followed the NMDPRA’s response to queries raised against it in the NEITI Oil and Gas Industry Audit Report covering 2021 to 2023. However, Senator Abdul Ningi, representing Bauchi Central, rejected the description of the differences as slight, noting that the figures showed substantial variations that required serious investigation. “The disparities in records of PMS importation between NMDPRA and NNPCL in 2022 and 2023, as stated in the NEITI Oil and Gas Industry Audit Report of 2021 to 2023, are too wide to be described as slight or being looked into without the seriousness required,” he said. Similarly, Senator Dayo Faduyile, representing Ondo South, said the discrepancies raised concerns about the reliability of the records submitted by the two agencies. He said the differences left room for questions about what might have gone wrong in the reporting of petroleum imports. Senator Anietan Bassey, representing Akwa Ibom North-East, called for a thorough investigation, insisting that Nigerians must not be shortchanged because of discrepancies in official records. “Mr Chairman and very distinguished colleagues, these questionable records of volume of PMS importation by the two agencies must be thoroughly investigated to save Nigerians from being yearly shortchanged and expose those milking the country dry,” he said. In his remarks, Dankwambo said the committee would convene a meeting involving the three agencies to establish the reasons for the conflicting figures. “In view of the unacceptability of presentations made by the representative of NMDPRA on queries raised against it in the NEITI Oil and Gas Audit Report covering 2021 to 2023, specifically on volume of PMS imported within the years under review, this committee resolved to summon heads of NMDPRA, NNPCL and NEITI for reasons behind the wide disparities,” he said. The committee is expected to use the meeting to seek explanations for the discrepancies and determine whether the records can be reconciled. Mourinho started with Vinicius, serving a four-match ban in La Liga, on the left flank and benched former Leipzig winger Diomande, despite his improving form. item.title: 2027: The Strength Of APC Is In Northern Nigeria – Basiru
item.description: The National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Ajibola Basiru, has described Northern Nigeria as the ruling party’s stronghold ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that both the region’s political elite and ordinary citizens support the party. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, Basiru expressed confidence in the APC’s prospects in the North, citing the support of prominent political figures and the establishment of a campaign office known as Arewa for Asiwaju. “The strength of the APC is in the Northern part of this country and you will see it by the grace of God when election comes in 2027. On Saturday, we had the leading lights in politics, in economy, in industry gathering together to donate a campaign office they call Arewa for Asiwaju. “Even some who are in the opposition party have changed, people like the former governor of Niger State Babangida Aliyu, now all of them are coming to join and work for the APC. The truth is that today, when you see the creme de la creme of Northern Nigeria, they are with us, you see the masses of Northern Nigeria are with us,” Basiru said. ﻿ The APC National Secretary also criticised opposition parties over their response to electoral defeats, saying they should learn to accept losses as part of the democratic process. Basiru said President Bola Tinubu had emphasised the need for politicians to accept both victory and defeat, adding that the APC had experienced losses in court cases and political contests but had moved on. “One of the things that our leader President Bola Ahmed Tinubu said is that anybody that wants that savour the joy of victory in a democracy must also be able to endure the pain when he loses. But in the case of Nigeria, it appears that the opposition only wants to win, they don’t want to lose. We have had our fair share of losses both in the court and in the political contests, and we have taken it, learn our lessons and moved on,” he said.
